payload.meets_need:
KILLER. The need was one sentence, and it is the sentence I have to answer honestly: a gate the owner must decide has to REACH them, be READABLE, and be DECIDABLE with one tap - and today it reached them as a card whose button errored.

What is demonstrated: the summons is tappable (every action URL asserted absolute across a real published card), the gate is legible on a lock screen (titled with iteration and gate, max priority, tagged), the decision is readable in full (a real brief sealed, published, confirmed servable, fetched back over the public internet and decrypted from the SERVED BYTES - run-a8e537c05cac, 10/10), the host holds nothing readable, and the owner is summoned exactly when the run would otherwise wait - which this iteration proves by its own conduct: nine gates walked, eight self-blessed under the delegation, NOT ONE pushed to the phone.

What is NOT demonstrated, stated plainly because the whole point of this iteration is that it was glossed over last time: the card rendering on the device and the tap firing. I cannot produce that evidence. It is D1, and it is the act that closes this gate's successor.

So: the need is met in every part I can evidence, and the one part I cannot is deliberately made into the release gate rather than claimed. Pass lines across all iterations hold - the i8 lane's seven checks still pass unchanged, so nothing earlier regressed to buy this.
payload.killers_demonstrated:
Two killers, from M5's own list.

S1 THE GATE ARRIVES AND CAN BE TAPPED - exercised as far as an agent can take it, and NOT further. Every published action URL is walked and asserted http(s) absolute in a real card built from a real offer (run-3a83f64d9dc6); the stub that reproduced the old 'answer:<topic>' made the check fail first, so it discriminates. The rendering and the tap are D1.

S2 THE DECISION IS READABLE - exercised END TO END AGAINST THE REAL WORLD, not a mock: run-a8e537c05cac against the actual Cloudflare account and worker. Seal a real gate brief, publish, CONFIRM SERVABLE (687ms - the design document assumed ~60s, so the measurement corrects the folklore), fetch the served page back, decrypt with the key from the link's fragment, and confirm the plaintext never appeared at the host. Served 200 text/html, so it renders rather than downloads. That is every step the owner's browser performs except the rendering.

Both killers therefore stop at exactly the same boundary - the physical device - and that boundary is the release gate. I am not counting the live run as covering D1: decrypting in Node with the same Web Crypto API is strong evidence, not the same act.
payload.acceptance_converted:
Converted, with one honest exception.

PERMANENT NOW - 19 checks in tests/i8d-brief.test.ts, one per requirement plus the promoted spike guards, all in the battery: absolute URLs, card shape, action budget, escaped brief, page carries ciphertext not plaintext, fragment-only key, confirm-before-announce both ways, bounded ttl, degrade-not-throw, degradation NAMED, announce recorded on success and failure, token absent from three surfaces, and the three R9 checks. Two deserve naming as more than tests: SP1's four negatives (wrong key, tampered payload, wrong tag position, url-safe charset) are the only thing standing between a shipped brief and a page that silently fails to decrypt on a phone - they were promoted from a spike precisely so they could never be lost. And the SOURCE-SCAN guard on bin/se-board.ts is a structural acceptance scenario: it fails if anyone ever reattaches the push to a timer, which is the mistake this iteration exists to undo.

NOT CONVERTED, with its reason: the live chain (run-a8e537c05cac) stays a demonstration rather than a battery check, because it needs real credentials and a live third party - putting it in the battery would make every run depend on a network and a token. Its unit-level equivalents ARE in the battery; what is not automatable is the realness, and that is the point of keeping it a demonstration.

D1 cannot convert at all. A tap is not automatable, and pretending otherwise is what shipped the broken button.
payload.consistency_swept:
Swept at sweep_consistency, five surfaces for five changes, and the sweep was driven by searching for the teaching surfaces rather than by recalling what I had touched.

The push rule is re-taught in se.guidance-phone-setup (a new section in the owner's own terms), in the node's STATEMENT (not only its body - the statement is what a reader sees in a list), and in se_wait's own TOOL DESCRIPTION, which is the surface an agent reads before any guidance and would have been the most expensive omission. The absolute-URL rule is taught where someone would otherwise reintroduce the bug: the manual-config section now says the topics stay BARE and are absolutized at send time. The brief store is documented from nothing, including its honest limit and an explicit statement that pairing alone is a COMPLETE rung. The board's narrowed role is corrected where the old text said it 'runs the lane'. The verify step is corrected - it previously would have had the owner waiting at a self-blessed gate for a buzz that correctly never comes.

The board's missing timer carries its reason in the code, and a test enforces the absence, so this sweep is guarded rather than merely written.

Deliberately unchanged: i8c's QR/deep-link surfaces, which this iteration did not touch.
payload.gaps_logged:
Four new RAID entries at log_gaps, each with kind, owner and a trigger naming a concrete fallback: se.raid-brief-store-unconfigured-is-silent (risk, agent - the gap this iteration CREATED: a store typo is indistinguishable from a deliberate opt-out, because I chose all-or-nothing whitelist loading; the whitelist stays, what is missing is a voice), se.raid-summons-is-single-channel (risk, OWNER - the unfilled slide behind Q1, owner-owned because only they can decide whether a second channel is worth building), se.raid-required-args-unvalidated-at-dispatch (issue, agent - a gap in the tooling that validated this work, found by being fooled by it), and se.raid-board-opens-a-new-tab-per-start (issue, agent, owner-reported mid-iteration, recorded with its diagnosis and with the honest note that suppression is cheap but the REFOCUS the owner asked for needs the live tab to raise itself).

The three M5 entries stand unchanged. Nothing from the story walk is unaccounted for: S1's unfilled half is D1, a demonstration bound to the release, not a gap being quietly deferred.
